## Summary

Both MATLAB/Acycle runs completed on the remote GitHub Actions MATLAB backend (R2024b). No retries were needed — every computation succeeded on first dispatch.

### Backend / provenance
- **Local MATLAB:** absent (`matlab_available: false`), but `remote_backend_configured: true`; backend = `github`, repository `JFjifang/Acycle_Harness`. Execution note confirms remote MATLAB is what runs. `python_numerical_fallback: false` — no numerical Python was used.
- **MATLAB source:** Acycle repo `https://github.com/mingsongli/acycle`, reference commit `dcba4279168745b563e0535b954297023dd62fc7`; installed commit identical. `all_used_sources_match_reference: true`. Verified functions (SHA-256 checked) include `RobotGUI.m`, `findduplicate.m`, `interpolate.m`, `acycleSamplingIsUneven.m`, `redconfML.m`, `rhoAR1.m`, `moveMedian.m`, `minirhos0.m`, `acycleMtmTaperCount.m`, `zeropad2.m`, `evofft.m`.
- **Environment:** MATLAB 24.2.0.3361896 (R2024b) Update 10 with Curve Fitting, Signal Processing, Statistics toolboxes. Numerical backend `MATLAB/Acycle`; plot backend "MATLAB (original redconfML plot; other GUI plots adapted)".
- **Remote dispatch:** baseline GitHub Actions run 40166934103, conclusion `success`, head_sha `0c5db90a…`, `acycle_revision` = the commit above. Robust fit method `original_redconfML`.
- **Input:** `/workspace/upstream/acycle/data/Examples/Example-WayaoCarnianGR0.txt`, 498 data rows / 7206 bytes, sha256 `f39dcc29be09cd5a07ef1dcdd20c6fa30499213c204ce4897ac02d9f6f086c21` (identical checksum consumed by both runs).

### Run IDs
| Role | Run ID | Parameters |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline | `20261025T054948Z-c2484cc8d88f` | lowess, span 0.35, evolution true, unit m |
| Sensitivity (child of baseline) | `20261025T055310Z-f5883a2371e6` | lowess, span 0.25, evolution true, unit m |

The baseline was preserved; the sensitivity run carries `parent_run_id = 20261025T054948Z-c2484cc8d88f`.

### Numerical findings
Preprocessing was identical and clean in both runs: 499 input rows → 0 non-finite removed, 0 duplicates merged, 498 processed rows, interpolation applied to a uniform 0.35341 m step. Nyquist 1.41477 cycles/m, nfft 2490, MTM NW 2, smooth fraction 0.25, evolution window 61.476 m with 0.70683 m step.

Baseline (span 0.35) top 10 spectral peaks, periods in **metres of stratigraphic thickness** (no age model supplied):

| Period (m) | Frequency (cyc/m) | Power | Pointwise >95% |
|---|---|---|---|
| 28.39 | 0.03523 | 268,855 | yes |
| 46.32 | 0.02159 | 249,293 | yes |
| 33.85 | 0.02955 | 243,876 | yes |
| 9.67 | 0.10341 | 233,569 | yes |
| 10.35 | 0.09659 | 183,728 | yes |
| 6.82 | 0.14659 | 168,943 | yes |
| 9.07 | 0.11023 | 140,763 | yes |
| 14.19 | 0.07045 | 133,997 | no |
| 12.94 | 0.07727 | 133,041 | no |
| 11.14 | 0.08977 | 124,814 | no |

Sensitivity span 0.25: 237,541 power at 9.67 m (now rank 1), 185,306 at 10.35 m, 169,465 at 6.82 m, 169,134 at 27.50 m, 143,607 at 9.07 m — these five are pointwise above 95%; 33.85 m (137,042), 14.19 m, 12.94 m, 44.00 m and 11.14 m fall below.

Effect of the span change:
- **Stable:** the four short-period peaks (9.67, 10.35, 6.82, 9.07 m) persist in both runs with pointwise >95% and essentially unchanged frequency bins; AR(1) background is nearly identical (ρ 0.62432 → 0.62341; s0 18,113 → 18,072), i.e. the red-noise model is insensitive to span.
- **Unstable:** the long-period cluster reorganises. 33.85 m loses pointwise significance, and the ~46 m and ~28 m peaks shift to 44.0 m and 27.5 m with reduced power, while 14.19, 12.94 and 11.14 m stay below threshold in both runs.
- Rank ordering of peaks is therefore span-dependent, so amplitude rankings should not be read as a robust hierarchy.

### Interpretation limits (explicit)
- Peaks are reported against **pointwise** 95% robust AR(1) levels; these do not control multiple testing, and the tool itself warns this is not proof of orbital forcing. No orbital-forcing or Milankovitch claim is made.
- The x-coordinate is metres of section (depth domain), so "periods" are thicknesses, not durations. No age model / sedimentation-rate conversion was applied, so no cyclicity in kyr can be asserted.
- The EvoFFT output retains mini-robot zero padding and normalized amplitude; edge windows contain synthetic zeros, so evolution-map edges are not trustworthy.
- This is a **tested numerical reproduction** of one Acycle mini-robot workflow on one file plus a one-parameter sensitivity check — not a reproduction of any publication, figure set, or stratigraphic conclusion. One span value is a minimal perturbation, not a full robustness sweep.

### Output paths
Baseline `20261025T054948Z-c2484cc8d88f` — `/workspace/Acycle_Harness/.acycle/runs/20261025T054948Z-c2484cc8d88f/`:
`outputs/cleaned.csv`, `prepared.csv`, `processed.csv`, `spectrum_robust.csv`, `spectrum_classic.csv`, `evolution.csv`, `preprocessing.png`, `spectrum.png`, `evolution.png`, `preprocessing.fig`, `spectrum.fig`, `evolution.fig`, `analysis.mat`, `provenance.json`; frozen input at `<run>/input.txt`.

Sensitivity `20261025T055310Z-f5883a2371e6` — `/workspace/Acycle_Harness/.acycle/runs/20261025T055310Z-f5883a2371e6/outputs/` with the same artifact set (e.g. `spectrum_robust.csv`, `spectrum.png`, `evolution.png`, `evolution_csv` → `evolution.csv`, `analysis.mat`, `provenance.json`).

- **Unstable:** the long-period cluster reorganises. 33.85 m loses pointwise significance, and the ~46 m and ~28 m peaks shift to 44.0 m and 27.5 m with reduced power, while 14.19, 12.94 and 11.14 m stay below threshold in both runs.
- Rank ordering of peaks is therefore span-dependent, so amplitude rankings should not be read as a robust hierarchy.

### Interpretation limits (explicit)
- Peaks are reported against **pointwise** 95% robust AR(1) levels; these do not control multiple testing, and the tool itself warns this is not proof of orbital forcing. No orbital-forcing or Milankovitch claim is made.
- The x-coordinate is metres of section (depth domain), so "periods" are thicknesses, not durations. No age model / sedimentation-rate conversion was applied, so no cyclicity in kyr can be asserted.
- The EvoFFT output retains mini-robot zero padding and normalized amplitude; edge windows contain synthetic zeros, so evolution-map edges are not trustworthy.
- This is a **tested numerical reproduction** of one Acycle mini-robot workflow on one file plus a one-parameter sensitivity check — not a reproduction of any publication, figure set, or stratigraphic conclusion. One span value is a minimal perturbation, not a full robustness sweep.
